newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister rules out forex policy change.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister rules out forex policy change.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir Tuesday ruled out any change in foreign exchange policy in reaction to currency woes in Asia and some other emerging markets.
Kandir told reporters he also regarded a sharp fall in Brazilian share prices as a short-term movement.
"We are not considering under any circumstance changing Brazilian foreign exchange policy," Kandir said.

The minister said falling share prices were partly caused by international players taking profits in order to cover their losses in Asia, where over the past two weeks Thailand and the Philippines have been forced into de facto devaluations.
The currencies of Indonesia, Malaysia and Poland have also come under pressure.

"The Asian crisis shouldn't affect Brazil," Kandir said, citing high foreign reserves, high privatization receipts and the prospect of economic growth as features that distinguished the Brazilian economy from its Asian competitors.
Kandir said the Brazilian government was "watching the situation with attention".

In contrast to Central Bank officials, the minister dismissed speculation that Brazil might even benefit from the woes of the Asian countries because international capital would find somewhere else to invest.
